subject: ventures/volunteer-shift-scheduler
professional: a volunteer coordinator who rosters a church, food bank or PTA every month (the Planning Center Services / SignUpGenius user); they check first that nobody is placed on a date they said they are away, nobody is over their limit or double-booked, that roles needing clearance (children's ministry, drivers) only go to cleared people, that every place that could be filled is filled, and that a change after one dropout does not reshuffle everyone's calendar

evidence.correctness: Hard constraints recomputed against my own code, not the author's validator. (1) /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/7a8bfab0-cf62-5b3b-91fe-5ee885a81cbd/scratchpad/vss/flow.mjs builds each random instance as a max-flow network (source->volunteer cap=max, volunteer->volunteer@day/slot cap 1, ->shift, shift->sink cap=headcount; Edmonds-Karp written for this audit) and compares seats filled: small instances (4-16 shifts, 3-13 volunteers, slots 'AM, PM') 0 of 20,000 worse than optimum at availability density 0.3 and 0 of 20,000 at 0.15; validateRoster ok on all. Larger instances (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/7a8bfab0-cf62-5b3b-91fe-5ee885a81cbd/scratchpad/vss/flow_big.mjs, 10-50 shifts, 5-30 volunteers, 12 days): 79 of 3,000 (2.6%) at density 0.3, 1 of 3,000 at 0.2, 158 of 3,000 (5.3%) at 0.12 leave exactly one seat empty that a feasible assignment fills (example: got 38, optimum 39); the unfilled line then reads e.g. '3 available: 3 at their max' as if the gap were forced. Never more than optimum, never invalid. (2) The sample/guide roster (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/7a8bfab0-cf62-5b3b-91fe-5ee885a81cbd/scratchpad/vss/misc.mjs) checked against the raw text of the ten volunteer lines with a hand-written rule table (not canDo): 0 violations, 19/19 filled, loads all 2 except Hugo (max 1) - matches the guide table row for row. (3) Weekly expansion 'Wednesdays 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-31' and 'Sundays 2026-03-01 to 2026-04-05' match Python's datetime weekday list exactly (9 and 6 dates). (4) parseTime 12am=0, 12pm=720, 12:30am=30; 2027-02-29 refused. (5) RFC 5545 s3.1 line length: with accented names a folded line is 81 octets (folding counts UTF-16 units, calc.mjs:437). Held at 3: every hard constraint holds and the solver is optimal on typical sizes; the sub-optimal fill on sparse larger rosters is a near miss, not a wrong number the page asserts.
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature exercised in node: slot parsing, shift lines with optional role/headcount and weekday repeats, volunteer availability (weekday, slot, weekday+slot, date, date range, any, weekends), max, not-roles, default max, greedy + repair + balance, unfilled reasons, over/under/idle/no-options flags, independent validator, roster CSV, by-volunteer CSV, whole and per-volunteer .ics, reminders with optional note, roster text, share link round trip (test 'share links round-trip'), local usage counters with opt-out and DNT/GPC. No TODOs or stubs. Performance at the limits: 300 volunteers x 416 weekly shifts built in 207 ms ({SP}/perf.mjs). The served page https://marisstella.app/volunteer-shift-scheduler/ could not be loaded from this session (proxy 403 on CONNECT, WebFetch ENOTFOUND), so deploy-time chrome is unverified; build_pages_site.rewrite_base_urls run locally rewrites llms.txt to marisstella.app correctly.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/volunteer-shift-scheduler && node --test '*.test.mjs': 48 tests, 48 pass, 0 fail (319 ms); bare `node --test` (README) also 48 pass. Good property tests (300 random rosters for hard constraints, repair never loses seats, guide table recomputed). Eight seeded mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 5 caught (balance gap 2->3, scarcest-first order reversed, fewest-shifts-first pick swapped with flex, over-loaded threshold +1, CSV formula guard removed), 3 survived: under-loaded flag < -> <= (calc.mjs:358, a flag shown on every row of the fairness table), time-overlap boundary < -> <= so back-to-back 9-12 / 12-3 shifts count as a clash (calc.mjs:223), and repair skipping any candidate with a clashing blocker (calc.mjs:290, the one-move swap the README describes). 3 of 8 surviving in core logic is below the bar.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (553 lines, pure, deterministic, input-order ties), index.html module script (~lines 150-283), usage.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Output escaped via esc() before innerHTML; share decode allowlists keys and caps length; CSV defuses formulas. Defects: slash dates are read as MM/DD only and the error hint uses the symmetric 10/10/2026 (calc.mjs:36, :122) so a UK/Canadian '05/11/2026' silently becomes 11 May; 'except' is a role-exclusion keyword (calc.mjs:191) so 'Sat; except 2026-10-24' becomes an excluded role and the person is still rostered on the 24th (only a misspelled-role warning); ics UIDs built from the sorted shift index and volunteer index (calc.mjs:455) change when a shift or volunteer is added, so a re-imported calendar can update the wrong event; folding by characters not octets (calc.mjs:437); the unfilled reason omits people already on the shift so its counts do not add up ('3 available: 1 at their max, 0 already booked', calc.mjs:344).
evidence.claims: Checked: 'never double-books / exceeds a maximum / respects availability and excluded roles' - backed (own checker, max-flow runs, 300-roster test). 'Unfilled places are listed with the reason' - backed, though the reason can imply a forced gap the solver merely missed. 'Balance ... never changes how many places are filled' - backed (take/give pair, calc.mjs:325). Guide FAQ 'no one carries two or more shifts above anyone else who could have taken them' - backed by the balance loop's stop condition. Guide worked example - reproduced exactly. 'Nothing is uploaded' / 'no analytics vendors' - backed (usage.mjs is localStorage only, no fetch). 'The calendar file opens in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook' (index.html:129) - plausible (VCALENDAR 2.0, floating local times) but not tested against any of them. Disclaimer, no-warranty, safeguarding caveat and share-link privacy warning present on page and guide. sitemap.xml:3-4 and robots.txt:4 use relative URLs, which the sitemaps protocol does not accept and the build does not rewrite (PLACEHOLDER_URL_RE matches only absolute hosts).
evidence.fitness: Walked a coordinator's month: ten volunteers, three Saturdays, four roles - the roster, gaps, per-person calendar and reminders come out in seconds and are right. Hit in the first hour: no blackout dates (availability is positive-only; 'except 2026-10-24' is read as a role and the person is still rostered that day); role clearance is opt-out ('not: Nursery') rather than opt-in, so a newly added, uncleared volunteer is eligible for children's or driving roles by default; no way to pin an assignment (team leader, a swap already agreed), so a rebuild after one dropout can move other people; frequency only as a total max (no 'once a month', 'not two weekends running'); no households/pairs serving together. Usable for a small one-off roster; a regular church or food-bank coordinator would keep a spreadsheet beside it.
evidence.domain: Compared with how volunteer scheduling is practised in the tools coordinators use (Planning Center Services, SignUpGenius, Ministry Scheduler Pro: blockout dates, position qualifications/teams, scheduling frequency preferences, household scheduling, locked/confirmed assignments) and with assignment practice (bipartite b-matching / max-flow gives a provably maximal fill). Matches practice on hard constraints and scarcest-first heuristics; departs on blockout dates, opt-in qualification for safeguarded roles, frequency rules, pinning, and an optimality guarantee (one-move repair, 2.6-5.3% of larger sparse instances one seat short).

mutations.change: a.start < b.end && b.start < a.end -> <= on both (back-to-back shifts clash)
if (blockers.length > 1) -> if (blockers.length >= 1) (repair never moves a clashing shift)

defects.what: 'except' is a role-exclusion keyword, so 'Sat; except 2026-10-24' (a blackout date) is read as an excluded role; the volunteer is still rostered that day with only a 'check the spelling' warning. No way to express blackout dates.
Slash dates are MM/DD only and the hint example 10/10/2026 is symmetric, so '05/11/2026' meaning 5 November silently becomes 11 May.
One-move repair is not a maximal fill: on 10-50-shift rosters 2.6-5.3% of random instances leave one seat empty that max-flow fills, and the reason line reads as if the gap were forced.
Three seeded mutations in core logic survive: under-loaded flag threshold, back-to-back time boundary, repair blocker rule. No test pins adjacency (9-12 then 12-3) or the under flag's boundary.

Role restrictions are opt-out only (not: Role); a newly added volunteer is eligible for every role, including safeguarded ones (children's ministry, driving), unless someone remembers to exclude them.
ics UID is built from the sorted shift index and volunteer index, so adding a shift or volunteer changes UIDs and a re-imported calendar can update the wrong event or duplicate it.
ics folding counts UTF-16 characters, not octets; accented names give 81-octet lines (RFC 5545 s3.1 says 75).
Unfilled reason omits people already on the shift, so the counts do not add up ('3 available: 1 at their max, 0 already booked').
sitemap.xml <loc> and robots.txt Sitemap: are relative ('./index.html'); the sitemaps protocol requires absolute URLs and the deploy rewrite only replaces absolute placeholder hosts, so this ships.

verdict: A clean, deterministic, private roster builder whose hard guarantees hold: in 40,000 small random rosters it never double-booked, never broke a max or role exclusion and matched an independent max-flow optimum every time, and the guide's worked example reproduces row for row. It misses the bar on verification (3 of 8 seeded core mutations survive, including the back-to-back time boundary) and falls short of a coordinator's real month on fitness and domain: no blackout dates ('except DATE' is silently read as a role), opt-out rather than opt-in role clearance, no pinned assignments, no frequency rules, MM/DD-only slash dates, and a one-move repair that leaves a fillable seat empty on 2.6-5.3% of larger sparse rosters. Finished (completeness 3), not meeting the bar (verification 2).
